headline: US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks, civilian casualties
summary: The US State Department has ordered non-emergency diplomatic staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. This follows recent deadly Houthi attacks on civilian targets, including an airport and an oil field, escalating regional tensions.
details: The US State Department has ordered non-emergency US government employees and their family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia. This decision comes amid escalating attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen on civilian targets within the country.

One person was killed and eight others injured in an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, according to Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority. Earlier, two people died after a drone attack on a facility at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield.

US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott stated that the Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, targeting civilian airports and critical infrastructure. These actions have resulted in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions.

The latest withdrawals follow an escalation of fighting in Yemen, opening another front in the regional conflict. This wider conflict was triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran in late February, impacting global energy trade and Gulf economies.

The US embassy in Riyadh had previously issued a security alert regarding possible further Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. This followed recent deadly strikes, including on Riyadh's airport and the embassy itself in early March.
US officials also indicated plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in other Gulf states, signaling a broader regional concern.

Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months after many were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities. This latest order reverses some of those recent deployments.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh eliminated from tri-series]] after 7-wicket loss to Afghanistan; Hridoy admits 'actions don't reflect words'
headline: Bangladesh eliminated from tri-series after 7-wicket loss to Afghanistan; Hridoy admits 'actions don't reflect words'
summary: Stand-in skipper Towhid Hridoy acknowledged the team's failure to perform in multi-nation tournaments, stating that their desire to win trophies isn't backed by on-field actions. He highlighted batting as the major issue in recent away matches.
details: Bangladesh has been knocked out of the ODI tri-series in the UAE following a seven-wicket loss to Afghanistan. Stand-in skipper Towhid Hridoy admitted the team's words are not always backed by their performances in major multi-nation tournaments.

Despite recent success against several teams at home, the Tigers have historically struggled to achieve their objectives in multi-nation events. This pattern was evident in both the 2023 ODI World Cup and the 2024 T20 World Cup, where the team failed to live up to expectations.

Hridoy stated in a press conference that while there is a collective hunger to win trophies in big series like the Asia Cup or World Cup, "We only say it, but our actions don't reflect it." This highlights a recurring challenge for the squad.

He specifically pointed to batting as the major issue, noting that the team's batting unit was dismantled in their second game of the tri-series. Hridoy clarified that the poor batting in the last two matches significantly impacted the entire team's performance.

Hridoy, who captained the series due to Litton Das's injury, observed that the team's batting has been consistently poor when playing away from home. He emphasized the need for professional players to adapt quickly to away conditions to prevent such batting collapses.

Looking ahead, Hridoy views the upcoming Asia Cup at home as a significant opportunity for the team to regroup and perform. He expressed hope that the team can meet the high expectations of their supporters.
He added that there is massive room for improvement in adapting to away conditions. The team needs to sit down and bring themselves to a good state to address these performance gaps.

Bangladesh had entered the tournament winning four of their last five ODI series at home, against teams like West Indies, Pakistan, New Zealand, and Australia. However, this was followed by an away loss to Zimbabwe in July, indicating a clear disparity in home and away performance.
